text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @alice (oncall) — elevated 429s detected for tenant SilverBrook (dedicated pool sb-prod-01). Spike started ~2026-03-15T02:12Z. 429 rate ~18% over baseline; errors impacting realtime endpoints /v1/generate. Auto-alert created: INC-3098765432.

alice (oncall): ack — I'm on it. assigning triage. Can someone grab tail logs + qps breakdown by route?

chen (sre): grabbing logs now. early look shows a sudden uptick in small concurrent sessions and repeated retries. KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x. happing across az-a and az-b. snippet of filter I used:

```
redwoodctl logs --tenant silverbrook --pool sb-prod-01 --since 10m --filter "status:429" | mlr head -n 200
```

maria (eng-runtime): quick thought — this looks like a burst of short sequences that defeat our prefix cache. two mitigations: 1) temporary contract rate override (enterprise) to raise qps for sb-prod-01, or 2) route a portion of traffic to sb-hot-2 (hot spare) while we stabilize. both have tradeoffs.

sam (acct_manager): we have authority to grant a time-limited override under SB-ENT-2023. we need expiry and a note for billing. I can approve a 2-hour bump if ops requests it.

alice (oncall): prefer routing to spare first (less billing fallout). chen — can you do a progressive reroute? start with 10% canary to sb-hot-2 and monitor 5m. If 429s fall, escalate to 100%. If not, we'll request override.

chen (sre): will do. plan: add route rule r-742 with weight 10 -> sb-hot-2, watch 5m. command:

```
redwoodctl route apply --from-pool sb-prod-01 --to-pool sb-hot-2 --tenant silverbrook --weight 10 --tag "INC-3098765432-canary"
```

incident-bot: automation note — route apply request received. executing.

incident-bot: route r-742 applied (10% to sb-hot-2). monitoring metrics: 429_rate (sb-prod-01): 18% -> 11% after 90s. sb-hot-2 seeing healthy token serve.

jordan (support): pinging SilverBrook: "We're seeing transient rate errors; we've routed a portion of your traffic to a warm spare to reduce errors. We'll follow up in 15m with status." (customer message queued).

alice (oncall): results look promising. keep canary for 10m, then move to 100% if stable. set a fail-safe rollback at +20m. chen, set SLO guard: if 429s on sb-hot-2 > 2% for 5m, rollback.

chen (sre): canary extended. adding guard. command to promote:

```
redwoodctl route promote r-742 --to-weight 100 --if-stable 10m --rollback-if "429_rate>2%"
```

maria (eng-runtime): if we need to promote and 429s persist, we'll request the contract override and coordinate traffic steering to dedicated backup pools in other regions. Also recommend capturing a sample of failing request traces for postmortem.

incident-bot: promotion triggered manually by chen at +9m: promoted to 100%. overall 429s dropped to 0.6% across endpoints.

alice (oncall): nice work. set mitigation expiry to 2 hours from now per sam's approval window. sam — can you confirm and note billing flag? :thumbsup:

sam (acct_manager): confirmed — approved 2-hour emergency bump if we need it, but since routing solved it we won't bill. I'll open a billing ticket and flag possible credit if we later need the override.

jordan (support): updated customer: "We're seeing normal traffic now. We've routed traffic to a spare and kept an emergency override on standby. We'll follow up with a formal incident summary and next steps."

alice (oncall): creating follow-up ticket: SRE-INC-3098765432, owners: chen + maria. action items: 1) postmortem (24h), 2) evaluate cache/kv misses and add workload-specific batching, 3) add a dedicated emergency routing playbook for SilverBrook.

maria (eng-runtime): adding a recommended runtime config: increase small-request batching threshold for sb-prod-01 and enable prefix prewarm for the top 50 routes. will attach config diff to ticket.

chen (sre): logs/artifacts saved under /artifacts/INC-3098765432. notes: no data plane errors beyond 429; no evidence of attack. probable legitimate traffic spike + client retries.

alice (oncall): wrapping — monitoring window active until +120m. if any regression, page same channel. thanks team. :rocket:
